title: [WL][ADC][HAL] Fix calibration: wait ADRDY (tSTAB) before writing calibration factor & disabling ADC to avoid HAL_ADCEx_Calibration_Start() timeout at low fADC
author: zudaR107
body:
## Summary

This PR fixes a corner case in `HAL_ADCEx_Calibration_Start()` for STM32WL where the ADC can get stuck in the enabled state (and the function times out on disable) when `fADC` is slow (e.g. HSI16 with a large asynchronous prescaler like DIV64).  
**Root cause:** we were writing the calibration factor and immediately issuing `ADDIS` without respecting the ADC enable/ready sequence and the stabilization time (`tSTAB`). When the APB/SYSCLK is much faster than `fADC`, the subsequent `LL_ADC_IsEnabled()` polling may spin until timeout.

## Technical details

- After averaging the calibration factor, the code now:
  1. Clears ADRDY,
  2. `LL_ADC_Enable(hadc->Instance)`,
  3. Waits for `ADRDY` (which guarantees `tSTAB` ≥ 10 ADC clock cycles),
  4. Writes the calibration factor when `ADEN=1` and `ADSTART=0`,
  5. Calls `LL_ADC_Disable(hadc->Instance)` and waits for the ADC to be effectively disabled (existing logic).

- This follows the activation/ready sequence described in the reference manual (ADC chapter: enable → wait for ready/stabilization → proceed). Waiting for `ADRDY` ensures the stabilization window is honored even when `fADC` is much lower than bus clocks.

- The change is minimal and preserves the HAL state machine and error code handling.

## Why this is needed

- With `ADC clock source = HSI16` and `ADC async prescaler = DIV64` the effective `fADC` is ~250 kHz.  
- The original code enabled the ADC, wrote the calibration factor, and disabled it immediately. On slow `fADC`, the peripheral might not have completed its internal stabilization/ready path; issuing `ADDIS` too early can lead to a condition where `LL_ADC_IsEnabled()` never goes low within `ADC_DISABLE_TIMEOUT`, returning `HAL_ERROR` and leaving `HAL_ADC_STATE_ERROR_INTERNAL`.  
- This manifested as a hard-to-debug failure **before** FreeRTOS start (calibration is typically done in `main()` before scheduler) and could cascade into unrelated driver issues.

## What changed (high level)

In `stm32wlxx_hal_adc_ex.c` (`HAL_ADCEx_Calibration_Start`), after computing the averaged calibration factor:
- Clear ADRDY
- `LL_ADC_Enable()`
- wait for `ADRDY` (with timeout)
- `LL_ADC_SetCalibrationFactor()`
- `LL_ADC_Disable()`
- existing wait loop for `LL_ADC_IsEnabled()==0`

This guarantees the proper enable/ready/stabilization sequence per RM.

## Backward compatibility

- No API changes.
- Behavior only becomes **more robust** across all ADC clock configurations.
- Tested to work both with slow `fADC` (e.g., HSI16 + DIV64) and with fast `fADC` (e.g., DIV1). With fast clocks the additional wait is negligible.

## Tests performed

- ✅ Reproduced the issue on slow `fADC` (HSI16 + DIV64): original HAL times out in `HAL_ADCEx_Calibration_Start()` waiting for `LL_ADC_IsEnabled()==0`.
- ✅ Applied this patch: calibration completes; no timeout; subsequent ADC use (including VREFINT/IN1 reads) works.
- ✅ Verified on fast `fADC` (HSI16 + DIV1): no regressions observed; calibration flow unchanged functionally.
- ✅ Verified that the HAL state machine and error codes remain coherent on success and on artificially forced timeouts (e.g., by reducing the ADRDY wait timeout).

- Board: ST50H with STM32WLE5JCI6
- Toolchain: CubeMX v6.15.0 / GCC v14.2.0 / Makefile
- Clocks: ADC clock source = HSI16, ADC async prescaler = DIV64 (problematic) and DIV1 (ok)

## Alternative considered

- Increasing `ADC_DISABLE_TIMEOUT` — does not solve the root cause; only hides the race when the ready sequence isn’t respected.

## Risks

- Minimal. Waiting for `ADRDY` is already the recommended activation/ready sequencing; on fast ADC clocks the extra wait is sub-millisecond.

## Links

- Related Issue: #7 (opened separately; describes reproduction and logs)
- Reference Manual: STM32WL, ADC chapter (activation/ready, stabilization time `tSTAB`, `ADRDY` flag). 

## Checklist

- [x] Code builds locally
- [x] Change is minimal and targeted
- [x] No public API changes
- [x] I will sign the STMicroelectronics CLA when prompted by the CLA bot

title: fix: missing HAL_PWR_DisableBkUpAccess in HAL_RCCEx_PeriphCLKConfig
author: flespark
body: missing `HAL_PWR_DisableBkUpAccess` in `HAL_RCCEx_PeriphCLKConfig` will result writing arbitrary data to RTC backup register when execute `__HAL_RCC_RTCAPB_CLK_ENABLE`

title: fix: missing HAL_PWR_DisableBkUpAccess in HAL_RCCEx_PeriphCLKConfig
author: flespark
body:
missing `HAL_PWR_DisableBkUpAccess` in `HAL_RCCEx_PeriphCLKConfig` will result writing arbitrary data to RTC backup register when execute `__HAL_RCC_RTCAPB_CLK_ENABLE`
